target_customer: Robotics teams training manipulation models that need real-world evaluation and recovery data
problem: Robot policies fail in real settings and teams lack physical environments and targeted data to find and fix failures. Enact runs policies, finds failure states and produces recovery datasets and evaluations.
business_model: Data and evaluation services for robotics model developers (pricing not public)
product_category: Real-world RL environments and recovery data for robotics

founders.name: James Stevens
founders.background_notes: YC page says he met Govind Chada at Stanford but lists no employers or degree.

founders.name: Govind Chada
founders.background_notes: Co-developed robot recovery methods published at robotics conferences, per launch post.

competitors.name: PhAIL (Positronic Robotics)
competitors.what: Real-world benchmark of robotics foundation models on commercial tasks

competitors.name: Robocurve
competitors.what: Independent benchmarks for robot AI models on real robots (YC S26)
competitors.traction_then: open source framework and a pilot

technical_complexity.rationale: Running physical environments, collecting recovery demonstrations and closing a training loop requires hardware, robotics research skill and in-house evaluation.

defensibility.rationale: Recovery data could compound, but evaluation and data competitors are already funded and robot labs can collect their own data.

market_need_then: Benchmarks like PhAIL show a gap between model performance and human operators, and the company says it is already serving robotics teams; no customers are named.

brand_strength.rationale: A Zurich robotics startup called Enact Intelligence raised $30M in October 2026 and dominates searches, which confuses the name; no brand evidence for this company.

outcome_analysis: Enact is an active Summer 2026 company with no outcome yet. A technical CTO from Stanford robotics research and Meta pairs with a CEO whose background is not documented. Name confusion with a better-funded Zurich company and funded evaluation rivals are early headwinds.
notes: No funding for this company found. The $30M pre-seed announced October 2026 belongs to Enact Intelligence (Zurich, Eta Robotics AG), a different company. A search summary credited James Stevens with a Stanford MS&E degree and early engineering at a $1.5B AUM startup, but the opened YC page did not state this, so it is not recorded.
